speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin our assessment, have you experienced any recent trauma or injury to that specific finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the mechanism of injury suggests a specific type of strain or fracture. Have you noticed any significant bruising, numbness, or an inability to straighten that finger since the incident?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger.

The mechanism of injury combined with your specific inability to actively flex the distal joint while it is extended at rest is highly characteristic of an extensor tendon avulsion at the base of the nail. Given the urgency, do you have access to an X-ray of the right hand, and if so, has it shown any displacement or fragmentation at the distal phalanx?

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
